location.description: an evidence-only DRAFT pre-release of NicoTM77/Mandatary (tag name `p120-evidence-v3`, no tag exists until a draft is published and it must never be published): not a product release and not a C5 release. A draft is visible to repository writers only; it is read through the GitHub API with `gh` (see docs/release-acceptance.md). The older drafts `p120-evidence-v1` and `p120-evidence-v2` are left unchanged.

notes: Git history limit: the raw evidence files were committed at f306a2a and fbb8193 of this pull request and are removed at the branch tip by additive commits. Their Git objects stay in the repository's history (the pull request's commits remain reachable through refs/pull/25/head) and are NOT purged; no history was rewritten. If the pull request is squash-merged they are not in main's history; the archive, not Git history, is the durable record.

An evidence-only draft release is durable for as long as the repository and the draft exist; an administrator can edit or delete it. The member manifest and the tarball digest committed here make any change detectable by the full audit; they cannot prevent deletion.

Version 2 supersedes version 1 without changing it: its manifest contains every one of the 131 members of `p120-evidence-v1` with the identical SHA-256 (`ARCHIVE.p120-evidence-v1.sha256` is the committed v1 manifest, so `report.py --check` proves this from the two manifests without reading either archive). v1 stays available in its own draft release.

Version 3 supersedes version 2 without changing it: its manifest contains every one of the 219 members of `p120-evidence-v2` (and therefore the 131 of v1) with the identical SHA-256 (`ARCHIVE.p120-evidence-v2.sha256` is the committed v2 manifest, so `report.py --check` proves this from the two manifests without reading either archive). v1 and v2 stay available in their own draft releases. Version 2 holds one description that review 520 found wrong (the README of `round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/` says the restart, crash and usage checks of that run did not execute); immutable archives are not edited, so the corrected description is the new member `round-4-fd69639/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5-corrected-README.md`.

dispositions.approved_by: Nico (repository owner), in the interactive session of 2026-11-17, option 1 of reviewer run 518 (review https://github.com/NicoTM77/Mandatary/pull/25#pullrequestreview-5930363145; recorded in the Kanban card of P1.20)
dispositions.decision: The existing interleaved A/B evidence is accepted as the owner-authorized disposition of R2, and SH-2d may be PASS WITH EXPLICIT DISCLOSURES once the report, criteria and disposition are consistent and independently reviewed. This is an acceptance-policy amendment, not a statistical result. No further statistical experiment and no broader behaviour change is part of this disposition.
dispositions.kept_visible: proof-drop runs 2/15 (arm A, no cache) against 0/30 (arm B, bounded continuity cache), one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.106 (original target p < 0.05 NOT met); contended `REL-LOAD-STABLE` passed in 0/15 A runs and 30/30 B runs, with 669 against 0 timeouts and 191 against 0 refusals of granted calls; clean 10 + 10 runs met every target (metadata reads per call -92.8 %, /info -99.8 %, daemon CPU per call -86.4 %, p95 not worse, 0 refusals/drops/timeouts in B); the original clean-host failures (3 of 5 VM runs, 18-68 % refusals) were NOT exactly reproduced in 16 later clean runs of the pre-cache product, although the mechanism (daemon saturation amplified by the service's own continuity reads, every proof drop a failed daemon read with about 50 calls in flight) is evidenced; the causal uncertainty is not removed. All clean and adverse results, the orphan arm-A contended run (kept, not counted) and the smoke-B run are preserved in the archive.
dispositions.not_claimed: that the pre-registered drop-rate statistic passed; that the original failures are exactly reproduced or exactly explained; any security waiver. Authorization, identity, invalidation, cancellation and fault classification, leases and freshness semantics are unchanged by this disposition; every denial that is a genuine unsafe or uncertain identity result stays a denial.
dispositions.reference: archive `round-2-fbb8193/docs/release/evidence/diagnostics/r2-ab/` (A/B per-run rows, raw runs, mutation results), `records/R2-RCA-report.md`, `records/review518-report.md`; docs/release-acceptance.md (R2 measurement)
dispositions.residual_risk: Under a saturated daemon the service can still refuse a legitimate call (403 safety_unverified, default_deny) or time out a daemon read: the failure is fail-closed (an availability risk, not an integrity or confidentiality risk), it is logged by the safety-transition diagnostics (`docker safety proof dropped` / `restored`, closed reason, no secret), and it is rarer and shorter with the bounded continuity cache (0 drops in 30 contended B runs).
dispositions.title: Intermittent fail-closed refusals of granted calls under the approved workload

findings.detail: The sealed report of the previous round failed `TestSecurityUIBrowser/recovery-reveal-phone` on Firefox (the Hide button at y = 852 below the 844 px fold). P1.20.1 (commit 70a4d63) fixed the layout only (pre-session top bar instead of a 144 px toggle row, compact reveal card on phones; scenario, assertions and viewport unchanged: the button is now at 760..804 in Firefox). In this evidence `browsers/*.log` show Chromium, Firefox and WebKit at desktop and 390x844 all passing, light and dark, on the clean worktree at the code commit. The earlier failing logs are kept in the archive (`round-1-f306a2a/`).
findings.title: Firefox recovery-reveal-phone (SH-9a): fixed by the P1.20.1 layout change; all six browser cells pass

findings.detail: technical-decisions.md 10.2 states the idle budget as "after startup" without a duration. In steady state the service is well inside it (27.8 MB after a first start, 33.3 MB when configured, 27.2 MB after a restart; `vm-amd64/release.json`, `footprint.idle`), and `REL-FOOT-SETTLE-*` passes. But every start (first start, restart, SIGKILL restart) first holds about 100 MB (100.55 MB peak after the first start, 98.81 MB after a restart) until 145-155 s, i.e. roughly twice the budget for two and a half minutes; the same figures were measured on both hosted CPUs (98-99 MB, settled at 140-160 s). It reproduces natively with the container's environment: with the SMTP relay configured, one heap allocation of about 64 MiB happens 85 ms after start (`GODEBUG=gctrace=1`: `94->94->88 MB`), and Go returns it to the OS only after the runtime's 2-minute forced collection. Not asserted here: which code path allocates it. A follow-up in the product (release the memory after the one-time work) would remove the transient; the harness records the whole curve and gates on the settle. R3 (owner decision): the steady-state definition of the idle budget (the maximum of the samples inside the final 60 s of a 300 s window) is accepted and documented in docs/release-acceptance.md; the transient itself is still reported (`REL-FOOT-SETTLE-*`).
findings.title: Start-up transient: about 100 MB resident for 2.5 minutes after every start

findings.detail: The adverse runs of the earlier rounds stay in the archive (`vm-diag-loop-1`, `vm-diag-loop-2`, `vm-run-1a01db9-full`) and stay FAIL in the criteria that name them. Evidenced (the root-cause report, archive `records/R2-RCA-report.md`; the mechanism, not the exact cause of the original clean-host failures, which was not reproduced): the fixture daemon saturates under the workload (dockerd and containerd about 165 % and 138 % of one CPU of 4) and the service multiplied its reads (12 per admitted status call, 33 per tail-logs call, every proof drop a failed daemon read with about 50 calls in flight). R2/B changed the product: one epoch-bound continuity check, at most one in flight, valid for less than 1 s, covers read admissions and stream deliveries; mutations, name resolution, target inspects and every authorization decision stay fresh (`docs/docker-backend.md`). The interleaved A/B measurement is in the archive (`diagnostics/r2-ab/README.md` is the guide): clean 10 + 10: metadata reads per call -92.8 %, `/info` per call -99.8 %, daemon CPU per call -86.4 %, p95 status 2.13 s -> 0.48 s and logs 5.99 s -> 0.49 s, 0 refusals/drops/timeouts in 10 B runs; contended (two host CPU burners) 15 A + 30 B: `REL-LOAD-STABLE` failed in 15/15 A runs and 0/30 B runs, timeouts 669 against 0, refusals 191 against 0, but the proof dropped in 2/15 A and 0/30 B runs (one-sided Fisher p = 0.106, target p < 0.05): the statistic the plan set for the drop rate alone is **not** met. The owner accepted this evidence as the disposition of R2 (section 6); SH-2d is therefore PASS WITH DISCLOSURES, not a pass of the statistic. The original clean-host failures were not exactly reproduced; the residual fail-closed availability risk is documented. The final VM run and both hosted runs of this evidence are clean (`REL-LOAD-STABLE` PASS).
findings.title: Intermittent fail-closed refusals under the approved workload on the slow VM daemon (R2): mechanism evidenced, bounded continuity cache measured, owner-approved disposition

findings.detail: `footprint.idle[configured].VmHWM_process_lifetime` is 178.07 MB on the VM (178.9 and 181.8 MB on the hosted runners): the setup, identity and matrix sign-ins (Argon2id, 64 MiB each) push the process above the 150 MB load budget briefly. The benchmark workload (API/MCP clients and log streams) contains no human sign-in and its measured peak is 41-43 MB with the high-water mark reset at the start of the window, so the budget is met as defined; a burst of sign-ins during load is not covered by this workload.
findings.title: Sign-in and setup raise the resident set to about 180 MB (outside the benchmark workload)

findings.detail: After a **clean** restore the manifest reports `agent_credentials 0` and `authenticators 2`; the two authenticators are the ones the restore itself retired locally (`restore report credentials_stripped: true`, no imported credential). docs/backup-restore.md says a clean archive carries no credential, which is true; the manifest field name suggests otherwise. The harness asserts the bearer-credential count and the report flag, not the sum.
findings.title: The restore manifest's `inactive_credentials` counts the installation's inactive records, not only the imported ones

findings.detail: (a) The hosted runners' `docker` buildx driver cannot export OCI, so on them the compressed image size is an **estimate** (every layer of `docker save` gzip-compressed at level 6; 12.29 MB amd64 and 11.66 MB arm64); on the VM the real OCI export gives 12 418 706 bytes and the estimator was calibrated against it at 0.15% on the same image (12 400 226 against 12 418 702 bytes). (b) The crash is a SIGKILL delivered to the service process from the host: `docker kill` is not used because the daemon treats it as a manual stop and never applies the restart policy. (c) The `--skip` option of the harness exists for diagnostics only; the final VM run of this evidence skipped nothing (`stage_seconds` has no `skipped`).
findings.title: Measurement notes

findings.detail: The raw evidence of the first two rounds (full harness JSON, raw logs, scan outputs, SBOMs, A/B raw runs: 72 files, about 124 000 added lines) is held in one versioned archive (`archive` in `catalog.json`) and removed from the branch tip by additive commits. The archive is an evidence-only draft release asset: durable while the repository and the draft exist, detectable but not preventable against deletion.

findings.detail: In the first VM run of the F2 fix (code commit 41ae8d5, archive `round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/vm-amd64/`) `PERSISTENCE-ERROR: DeployError: login step 2: 403` ended the persistence stage. What ran before it PASSED in that run: REL-RESTART-1..4, REL-CRASH-1, REL-CRASH-2, REL-USAGE-AFTER-CRASH and REL-USAGE-RING-AFTER-CRASH (an earlier text of this finding and the README of that archive member said they did not execute; that was wrong, see `round-4-fd69639/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5-corrected-README.md`). Only the final administrator re-sign-in after the SIGKILL stage failed. The mechanism is a defect of the harness's period bookkeeping, reproduced RED to GREEN and fixed at fd69639, closed as a stated remediation (section 6, F5 of review 520) and kept as an adverse ref of SH-7a, P1-E3 and P1-E4. Not established: that the boundary straddle happened in that very run (no timestamps were archived); a recurrence with the corrected harness would be investigated as a possible product defect. The same stage passed in the VM runs at 2ac064f and fd69639 and on every hosted run of that product.
findings.title: One `login step 2: 403` at the administrator's final re-sign-in of one VM run: a harness defect (TOTP period read before the verifier spends its own)

findings.detail: The first run of the new `REL-STOP-LONG` check passed its product assertion (REST stop answered 200 after 12.2 s on the VM and on both hosted CPUs, before the fix the same shape is an EOF/502) and failed only because `tests/release/mcpclient` reported `elapsed_ms` 0 for every step (a deferred assignment on an unnamed result). The check is deliberately fail-closed on an unmeasured MCP answer; the client was fixed (named result) and the check re-run at 2ac064f. Both runs are archived (`round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/`).
findings.title: The first runs of the F2 fix are kept, not hidden: REL-STOP-LONG found a defect in the test client

details: Contract, gates, freshness guard and verification steps: docs/ci-image-publication.md; hermetic tests: tests/publish/ and scripts/ci-budget.test.mjs.

Dry run (NOT GHCR): the publication script was run end to end against a throwaway local registry on the isolated test VM (Docker 29.9.3, containerd image store, two real commits): first publication, repeat run, newer commit, stale older commit (see docs/ci-image-publication.md). It proves the command sequence and parsing, not GHCR, authentication, package association or the hosted runner's Docker. The log is the supplemental asset `p120-publish-dryrun-v1.log` of the evidence-only draft release (SHA-256 4c1cfa30721be3e57e45642fb22d371592013bb7c8bcf7e581105030f7fd587e; not an archive member).
The first real publication is verified by reading the registry (gate G-GHCR); a green pull request run is not evidence of it.
publication.status: **Registry publication: NOT EXECUTED.** Nothing was pushed to a registry, and a pull request run cannot publish: the CI workflow publishes `ghcr.io/nicotm77/mandatary:dev` only from a successful `push` to `refs/heads/main` of `NicoTM77/Mandatary`, after every required gate of that exact commit (both architecture jobs included) succeeded. This card does not merge, deploy or run the publishing job.

remediations.adverse_run: hosted CI run 44003552068, job `Image (linux/amd64)` (head e5e1856, merge commit 0d6b022fc1d1b180092ac87fd2409a0c85422b3e): `REL-MATRIX-REST`, `REL-MATRIX-PARITY` and `REL-MATRIX-POS` FAIL, X-dn-stop-A: REST `(502, '', '')`, MCP 200. The product of that run was identical to the product the earlier evidence judged, so one of four hosted runs of that product failed. Archive root `adverse-ci-e5e1856/`; the run was omitted from the first version of this evidence (review 519 F1) and is now recorded as an adverse run of the criteria that cite those checks.
remediations.finding: Review 519 reproduced a product defect on the same call shape: `cmd/mandatary` set a 10 s `WriteTimeout` on every response while an admitted one-shot stop or restart may run `timeout_seconds` plus a 15 s stop grace (10 + 15 s by default, up to 315 s). The server closed the connection before the handler wrote its result, so the client saw EOF (behind the proxy an empty-body 502) although the stop completed and was counted allowed. The harness then recorded no per-call timing, so it cannot be shown from the archived run that its X-dn-stop-A call exceeded 10 s.
remediations.fix: Narrow, after authorization only: the ops service announces the dispatch bound of an admitted stop/restart (`ops.DispatchObserver`, only for those two operations, only after authorization and the expired-bound check); the REST and MCP transports then extend that one response's write deadline to bound plus 5 s (`api.WithAdmissionDeadline`, forward only, read deadline untouched). Unauthenticated, denied and invalid requests keep the 10 s bound. No authorization, identity, invalidation, lease or freshness semantics changed. Documented in docs/api-mcp.md and docs/operations.md.
remediations.fresh_evidence: At the code commit 2ac064f: the VM run (`vm-amd64`) 156 PASS / 0 not PASS and both hosted CPUs (`ci-amd64`, `ci-arm64`, hosted run 44059883746) 156 PASS / 0 not PASS: `REL-MATRIX-REST`, `REL-MATRIX-PARITY`, `REL-MATRIX-POS` and `REL-STOP-LONG` PASS on all three (the REST stop answered 200 after 12.2 s on every CPU). The matrix timing of the VM run shows the slowest matrix stop/restart at 5.3 s.
remediations.not_established: that the write bound was the cause of the one hosted 502: the archived run has no per-call timing and the failure did not recur (the hosted runs 44044826495 at 45629a3, 44055078430 at 41ae8d5 and 44059883746 at 2ac064f all passed `REL-MATRIX-REST`), so the cause of that single 502 is not established. The write-bound defect is real and fixed; the remediation closes the criteria on fresh passing evidence and does not prove that this was the cause. A later hosted 502 of the same shape would reopen it.
remediations.reference: review 519 (`records/review519-report.md`, https://github.com/NicoTM77/Mandatary/pull/25#pullrequestreview-5935593688); docs/api-mcp.md (Stop and restart outlive the 10 s server write bound); archive `adverse-ci-e5e1856/`, `round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/`
remediations.tests: RED-to-GREEN through the real `serverFor`, REST and a real MCP client against a slow executor (`cmd/mandatary/stop_write_deadline_test.go`: an admitted stop and restart deliver their result past the 10 s bound; unadmitted requests keep it), the ops observer tests (`internal/ops/dispatch_observer_test.go`: announced only after authorization and only for stop/restart), the transport unit test (`internal/api/admission_deadline_test.go`), and hand/script mutation checks of the wiring. The release harness gained per-call REST/MCP timing in the matrix stage and the `REL-STOP-LONG` check (container A ignores SIGTERM, `timeout_seconds` 12: REST stop, start and the MCP restart must still answer 200 although they outlast the 10 s bound, and A must run again; an unmeasured or fast answer is a failure); its fail-closed behaviour has positive and eight negative unit twins (`tests/release/test_release.py`).

remediations.adverse_run: the VM run at 41ae8d5 (archive `round-3-2ac064f/diagnostics/run-41ae8d5/vm-amd64/`, summary `adverse-vm-41ae8d5`): `PERSISTENCE-ERROR: DeployError: login step 2: 403`. The product of that run was identical to the product of the later code commits. The same stage passed in the next VM run (2ac064f) and on every hosted run of that product. REL-RESTART-1..4, REL-CRASH-1/2, REL-USAGE-AFTER-CRASH and REL-USAGE-RING-AFTER-CRASH all PASSED in the failing run; only the final administrator re-sign-in after the SIGKILL stage (`tests/release/ops.py`, the last statement of `persistence()`) was refused. It is an adverse ref of SH-7a, P1-E3 and P1-E4 (the criteria that rest on the persistence stage and on administrator TOTP sign-in); the earlier text that the restart, crash and usage checks of that run did not execute was wrong and is corrected (finding F-8).
remediations.finding: A defect of the test harness, not of the product. `Admin.login` (`tests/release/stackdeploy.py`) remembered the TOTP period from BEFORE it posted step 2, but the service records an accepted code under its OWN verifier period, taken when it verifies, and refuses any later acceptance in or before a recorded period (`internal/auth/lifecycle.go` VerifyTOTP, `HasTOTPReplay`: `verifier_period >= period`; `docs/authenticator-lifecycle.md`). A step 2 in flight across a 30 s boundary (code computed in period P, verified in P+1) therefore spent P+1 while the harness believed P was spent; the next sign-in, already in P+1 and started within 30 s, was correctly refused as a replay. The same ordering existed once more in `complete_setup` (period read before the confirm request). The sign-in that failed is the one that follows REL-RESTART-3's sign-in by less than 30 s (restart, crash and usage reads in between), the only place of the stage where two sign-ins are that close.
remediations.fix: Test code only (`fd69639`): the period is read after the step-2 answer, which follows the verification, and advances even when step 2 is refused; the setup path reads its period after the confirm answer. No product file changed (the product diff against 2ac064f is empty outside test files; the only product-side addition is the regression test below, which pins the rule the harness relies on).
remediations.fresh_evidence: At the code commit fd69639 (round 4): the VM run 156 PASS / 0 not PASS including the persistence stage and its final re-sign-in, and both hosted CPUs (hosted run 44074980728) 156 PASS / 0 not PASS. Every check of SH-7a, P1-E3 and P1-E4 passes on all of them.
remediations.not_established: that the boundary straddle actually happened in the failing run: the archived run carries no timestamps of its two sign-ins, so the straddle is inferred from the failure signature and from the deterministic reproduction, not observed. The mechanism is evidenced (reproduced against a stand-in of a rule that the real product test pins), the failure of the run is consistent with it, and no other cause was found; it is a harness defect for which a recurrence with the corrected harness, which now also records the refusal's closed code/reason and the TOTP period, would reopen the question as a possible product defect. A rare straddle probability (a window of milliseconds in 30 s) is plausible for one run in a few, not proven for this one.
remediations.tests: RED to GREEN with a fake clock and a stand-in for the service's rule (`tests/release/test_release.py` AdminLoginPeriod): a step 2 that crosses a boundary makes the next sign-in fail with `login step 2: 403` on the previous harness (RED, the exact signature of the run) and succeed on the fixed one (GREEN, it waits for the period after the verifier's); a non-straddling sign-in still waits only for the next period; the stand-in itself refuses a second acceptance in one period (negative control); a refused step 2 still advances the remembered period. The service rule is pinned against the real product by `internal/auth` `TestTOTPPreviousStepCodeSpendsTheVerifierPeriod` (a code of the previous step accepted in period P spends P; a second acceptance in P is refused; the next period accepts; killed by a mutant that records the code's step instead of the verifier period) and by the existing `TestTOTPConcurrentReplayAndPeriodLimit`.
remediations.title: VM run at 41ae8d5: `login step 2: 403` at the administrator's final re-sign-in (a harness defect)

verdict_notes: Every PASS below is read from a recorded result of the named check in the named archived document; the digest shown is the SHA-256 of that RAW document, taken from `docs/release/evidence/ARCHIVE.sha256` and bound to the committed summary (`report.py --check`).
A browser engine, architecture, or scanner that was not run is UNVERIFIED, not PASS. Where a result is FAIL the failing evidence is in the archived document and in section 8.
arm64 was exercised only by the hosted arm64 runner (no arm64 VM exists). The Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 13 / Unraid hosts were not exercised by this report.

The browser suites and the local gates ran on the coder's controller host on a clean worktree at exactly the code commit (`gates/tree-before.txt`, `gates/tree-after.txt` in the archive); the harness run is on the isolated VM from a `git archive` of the same commit. The hosted CI run is at the same code commit.

The R2 A/B runs (archive `diagnostics/r2-ab/`) are diagnostics with the load-independent stages skipped (`--skip`, diagnostics only); they are not evidence for a criterion, and the final VM run of this evidence skipped nothing.

SH-2d is PASS WITH DISCLOSURES only because of an owner-approved acceptance-policy disposition (section 6). It is NOT a claim that the pre-registered proof-drop statistic passed: it did not (2/15 against 0/30 runs with a drop, one-sided Fisher p = 0.106, target p < 0.05). The historical adverse runs stay FAIL.
